title: Adaptive status and customer postmortem playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a customer-facing communications playbook for incidents affecting Redwood Inference customers. It contains short status-page-ready blurbs, expanded incident summaries suitable for customer emails, and a template-style postmortem summary written for external customers. The document is intentionally pragmatic and modular so CS/SRE can cut-and-paste variants by severity and customer tier.

Notes to self / intent:
- Keep public timeline high level but accurate; internal timelines live in the incident timeline doc (JIRA/INC).
- Provide clear customer impact statements and suggested mitigations/workarounds where applicable.
- Surface the expected remediation timeline and concrete next steps (what we will do, what customers may optionally do).
- Include FAQ section to address common customer concerns.
- Draft should be editable by CS lead + SRE tech lead.

Status page short update (<= 280 chars):
- Initial: "We are aware of degraded inference performance in region <REGION>. Our team is investigating. Some requests may see increased latency or errors. Check this status page for updates."
- During recovery: "Partial recovery in <REGION>. Traffic being routed to healthier capacity; some customers may still experience elevated latency. Investigating root cause and validating data integrity."
- Resolved: "Service restored for <REGION>. All systems healthy. If you see persistent issues, please open a support ticket with request IDs and timestamps."

Status page detailed update (longer, public):
- Title: Inference latency surge affecting <REGION> (start: <ISO_TIMESTAMP>)
- Summary: Starting at ~<HH:MM UTC> we observed a sustained increase in inference latency across a subset of nodes serving <MODEL_OR_MODEL_FAMILY>. Requests exceeding typical p95 by 2-5x and increased error rates for long-sequence workloads. Impact duration: ~<hours>.
- Customers affected: Tenants routed to <POOL/QUEUE> in <REGION>. Dedicated customers on pinned capacity not in <POOL> were mostly unaffected.
- Mitigation steps taken: 1) Triaged faulty autoscaling behavior and temporarily increased burst capacity; 2) Deployed config rollback for recent kernel selection change; 3) Routed traffic to fallback model variant for latency-sensitive routes.
- Current status: Partial recovery, throughput improving, lingering elevated p99 for very-long sequences.
- Next updates: ETA ~30-60 minutes for full recovery verification, or earlier if status changes.

Customer email / post-incident summary template (customer-facing):
- Subject: Update: Service impact on inference latency in <REGION> — timeline & actions

Hi <Customer-Name>,

We want to share a summary of the incident that impacted inference latency for requests routed to <REGION> on <DATE>. Our priority was to restore service while preventing data loss and minimizing inconsistent outputs. Below is a concise summary you can use internally.

1) Impact summary:
- What happened: Starting at <ISO_TIMESTAMP> a change in autoscaler heuristics combined with an atypical sequence-length distribution caused burst scaling delays and a subset of nodes to experience degraded kernel selection behavior, increasing latency and error rates for some requests.
- Who was affected: Requests from tenants routed to <POOL> and workloads using <MODEL> with sequences > <N> tokens. Dedicated-reserved pools with pinned nodes were not impacted.
- Severity: P2 (customer-visible latency spike, no confirmed data loss).

2) Customer-facing timeline (public):
- <ISO_TIMESTAMP> — Spike detected; alerts triggered and initial paging.
- +12m — Scoped to autoscaler + kernel selector interaction; mitigation plan drafted.
- +35m — Quick rollback of kernel-selection change and increased burst capacity.
- +1h10m — Traffic partially routed to fallback model variant; p95 back to target for most requests.
- +2h00m — Monitoring confirms stability; service declared recovered after verification period.

3) Root cause (high level):
- Contributing factors: Recent kernel-selection optimization deployed on <DATE>, autoscaler configuration that underestimated effective capacity for high-sequence workloads, and a traffic pattern shift from one major customer that increased long-sequence request proportion.
- Root cause statement: A combination of a model-serving kernel change and autoscaler tuning led to transiently insufficient execution capacity during a traffic composition shift.

4) Remediation & follow-up actions (what Redwood did):
- Rolled back the kernel-selection change within 30–40 minutes.
- Adjusted autoscaler headroom thresholds and burst allocation for long-sequence pools.
- Added a safety route to fallback model variants when p95 latency breaches thresholds for >5 minutes.
- Added new alerts to detect composition shifts (token-length distribution anomalies) and automated a limited pre-warm for high-sequence spikes.

5) Customer actions & mitigations (recommended):
- If you rely on low-latency long-sequence responses, consider: 1) using the fallback model variant for tail-sensitive endpoints, 2) sending optional sequence-length hints in request metadata ("estimated_tokens": <n>) where supported to allow better routing, 3) enabling retry/backoff with jitter for non-idempotent flows.
- If you saw truncated or error responses, please share sample request IDs and timestamps; we will prioritize replay and verification.

6) SLA & credits:
- Impact classification: We have evaluated this as a latency SLO breach for specific routed tenants. If you believe this incident impacted your contractual SLA, open a ticket and include impacted window and example requests; CS will route for SLA review.

7) What we will do next (actionable commitments):
- Complete a full technical postmortem documenting the timeline, root cause analysis, code/config changes and precise regression tests. Expected delivery: <DATE_PLUS_7_DAYS>.
- Patch deployment to autoscaler + kernel-selection guardrails. Expected ETA: <DATE_PLUS_3_DAYS>.
- Follow-up customer webinar for enterprise customers explaining long-sequence routing best practices (optional).

FAQ (customer-focused):
Q: Could my data have been lost or corrupted?
A: No evidence of data loss or corruption. We validated persisted payload paths and storage logs. If you have a specific request id you are concerned about we will replay the request and confirm integrity.

Q: Why did fallback model outputs differ from the primary model?
A: Fallback variants are functionally equivalent but tuned/quantized differently for latency — you may observe minor output differences. We only route to fallbacks when latency-risk thresholds are crossed to avoid wider regressions.

Q: How can I avoid affecting my users during incidents?
A: Recommended: add retries with exponential backoff for non-real-time flows, optionally fall back to cached responses for known prompts, and for mission-critical low-latency paths, pin to dedicated capacity or a reserved inference pool.

Communication templates by severity (cut & paste):
- P1 short: "We are investigating a service disruption impacting inference in <REGION>. Our initial mitigation is routing traffic to healthy capacity; expect updates every 15 minutes."
- P2 short: "We’re seeing elevated latency for specific workloads in <REGION>. Workarounds deployed; monitoring. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary."
- P3 short: "Intermittent errors observed for a small subset of background/batch jobs; workaround available. See steps below to replay."

Internal playbook checklist (for CS + SRE co-ordination):
- [ ] Confirm impacted customer list via routing metadata.
- [ ] Prepare initial short status blurb and publish to status page.
- [ ] Identify enterprise customers on SLAs; notify CSM and account execs with tailored note.
- [ ] For each impacted tenant: collect example request IDs and timestamps.
- [ ] Decide on routing mitigations (fallback model, reroute, increase capacity) with SRE lead.
- [ ] Draft customer email using template above; get SRE tech lead signoff on root-cause language.
- [ ] Publish postmortem to customers within 7 business days (or accelerated if high severity).
